title: Send clears the Paper draft once the record holds that paper
evidence: desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:519-534 keeps and restores the draft per learner; desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx:70 (before) `onClick={() => void post({ type: "paper.enter", ... })}` - nothing cleared it; desk/src/lib/session/learners.ts:480-489 addPaper appends (PAPERS_CAP 5). tools/paper-aim-test.cjs:421 draft 1.
body:
## Summary
The phone's Paper draft was never cleared on Send, so a reload restored a paper the desk had already kept and Send wrote it again (hand-off from maths-school).

## Description
rules/paperDraft (maths-school) keeps the Paper rows per seated learner in localStorage; desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:519-534 writes and restores them. desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx posted `paper.enter` and left the rows, so the stored draft outlived the paper it became: a reload restored it and a second Send called addPaper again (desk/src/lib/session/learners.ts:480), a duplicate taking one of the learner's five kept papers. Fixed: PaperPanel's Send goes through `sendPaper` (desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx:35), which clears the rows to one blank row (and so the stored draft) only when the answering session's newest paper is exactly what these rows make (cleanPaper items and unmapped).

## Flow
- learner types a paper on the phone, Send
- desk keeps it (addPaper), the TV shows the recovery list
- phone reloads: the draft is restored and Send writes the same paper again
- fix: sendPaper compares the response session's paper with the rows and clears the draft only then

## Expected impact
A learner (or a parent) reloading the phone no longer sends the same paper twice and loses a kept paper slot to a duplicate. Could break: a kept paper whose items differ from the rows (the desk re-cleans them the same way, entryOf = cleanPaper) would leave the draft, the old behaviour.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a sent paper is not restored and re-sent after a reload
Before: a kept paper cleared the draft 0/1 (tools/paper-aim-test.cjs draft 1, red)
After: kept paper clears 1/1; the five non-kept answers (409, throw, not saved, no row, empty body) clear 0/5
Method: gate - sendPaper run against stub posts and the real addPaper on a temp DESK_DATA_DIR
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A Paper send clears only the rows it sent, not rows typed while in flight
evidence: registry software-engineering/draft-editing technique draft-model: "It remembers what it sent... drafts keep moving while saves are in flight". desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx:41 clears only when `JSON.stringify(now()) === JSON.stringify(rows)`; :82 the live ref. tools/paper-aim-test.cjs:457 draft 3.
body:
## Summary
The first draft fix (9c228909) cleared whatever the panel held when the send resolved, wiping a row typed while the post was in flight.

## Description
Registry draft-editing, technique draft-model: clean is decided against the payload that was actually sent, because drafts keep moving while saves are in flight. sendPaper compared the session's paper with the sent rows but then cleared the current draft whole. Fixed: sendPaper takes the panel's live rows (desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx:82, a ref) and clears only when they still equal the rows it sent (:41).

## Flow
- learner taps Send, then adds a question before the answer returns
- the answer holds the sent paper
- before: the draft, including the new question, is cleared
- after: the draft stays, so the new question can be sent

## Expected impact
A row typed during a slow send is not lost. Could break nothing visible: an unchanged draft clears exactly as before.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - in-flight edits survive the clear
Before: a draft that moved during the send cleared 1/1 (draft 3 red)
After: moved draft cleared 0/1; unchanged draft cleared 1/1
Method: gate - paper-aim-test draft 3 with a live-rows getter
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A refused or lost Paper send says so on the phone
evidence: desk/src/app/api/session/route.ts:66 answers 409 NOT_ASKING to a phone paper with no open paper ask, without dispatch (no status). desk/src/app/phone/panelFor.ts:131 deskLine is the phone's rule (phone-surface c2b7d59b, 3abb7695). desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx:35-43 sendPaper now returns the line; :103 shows it. tools/paper-aim-test.cjs:442 draft 2.
body:
## Summary
The Paper panel's Send showed nothing on a 409 refusal or a send that never arrived, while every other phone send follows deskLine / "That did not reach the desk.".

## Description
The phone has one send rule (desk/src/app/phone/panelFor.ts:131 deskLine; brought to page.tsx by phone-surface today): a refusal says its own line, no answer says "That did not reach the desk.". PaperPanel's Send was `void post(...)`: the 409 "The TV is not asking for that now." (desk/src/app/api/session/route.ts:66) is answered before any dispatch, so no session status carries it, and a fetch that threw was an unhandled rejection. Fixed: sendPaper returns the line (desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx:35-43) and the panel shows it in a role=status paragraph (:103), cleared on the next Send; an answered paper still says its status through the session.

## Flow
- TV closes the paper ask (Back) while the learner types; learner taps Send
- route answers 409 NOT_ASKING; nothing changes on the phone
- fix: the panel says "The TV is not asking for that now."
- phone offline: the panel says "That did not reach the desk."

## Expected impact
The learner learns the paper was not taken and why, instead of assuming it went. Could break: a stale line until the next Send (cleared there).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every failed Paper send leaves a line
Before: failure kinds with a line on the phone 0/3 (409 with error, 403 without, throw)
After: 3/3; answered sends adding a line 0/2 -> 0/2
Method: gate - paper-aim-test draft 2
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Tonight's Marked card promised a first one to look at when every ring was fixed
evidence: desk/src/tv/mathsRows.ts:127-133 continueCard: caption by `right === n` only; focus = firstToLook (desk/src/tv/sheetRows.ts:41-44, counts second === "right" as fixed). tools/maths-second-test.cjs:239 case 8c.
body:
## Summary
continueCard chose its caption by "all right first time" while Enter lands by firstToLook, so a fully fixed set read "on the first one to look at" and landed on Six more.

## Description
desk/src/tv/mathsRows.ts:127-133: the Marked card's caption was "All ... came back right" only when every first attempt was right, else "Enter shows it again, on the first one to look at." Its focus is firstToLook (desk/src/tv/sheetRows.ts:41), which skips items whose second go held; with every ring fixed it is items.length, the Six more stop. Fixed: a third caption when lookCount is 0 - "Every one to look at is fixed now. Enter shows the set, and six more are one press away." The hero line keeps the first attempt (GUARD case 8).

## Flow
- set marked with items 2 and 4 wrong; learner fixes both on the phone (second go)
- Tonight: the Marked card says "on the first one to look at"
- Enter lands on Six more, past the tiles
- fix: the caption names what is there

## Expected impact
The caption stops promising a place that is not there. Could break: nothing else reads the caption.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the caption matches where Enter lands
Before: captions promising a first one to look at on a fully fixed set: 1 (case 8c red)
After: 0; the nothing-fixed, one-fixed and all-right captions unchanged
Method: gate - maths-second-test case 8c
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Tonight's Marked card draws a held second go as the sheet does
evidence: desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx:853 Tally and :918 MarkedItem draw data-second and the tick (maths-tv-test second 1-4); desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx:524-536 Hero did not (box said "look again", tally a bare ring). tools/maths-tv-test.cjs:1439 second 5.
body:
## Summary
Two of the three places that draw a marked item (Sheet, Walk) show a held second go; Tonight's Marked hero still said "look again" on a fixed item.

## Description
challenge math-buddy-B taught the Sheet's and Walk's tally (desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx:853) and number (:918) to keep the ring and wear a tick for `second === "right"`. The Hero (:524-536) was the un-migrated call site: the box wrote "look again" in the pen's hand and the tally drew only the ring. Fixed: the box carries data-second and draws the tick in place of the word (ring kept); the tally draws the tick over the ring in the same 48 px (.tally .held in desk/src/design/maths-lamplight.css), so the tally keeps its width.

## Flow
- learner fixes item 2 on its second go; goes back to Tonight
- the Marked card's box 2 says "look again", its tally a ring
- fix: ring plus tick, as the sheet draws it

## Expected impact
Tonight agrees with the sheet the learner just left. Could break: tally layout - the tick overlays inside the same 48 px box; a capture is owed.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one picture of a held second go on every surface
Before: sites drawing a held second go 2/3; "look again" on a fixed box 1
After: 3/3; 0
Method: gate - maths-tv-test second 5 (server render)
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Hold the whole Lamplight stylesheet to its 28 px floor, not only the scripts
evidence: docs/DESIGN-MATH-BUDDY.md:50 law 8; tools/maths-type-test.cjs:300 test 19 reads only .sup/.sub/.msq-i/.mf.l/.mf.s; stylesheet: 96 px font-size selectors, 23 under 28 px, 7 of them non-label reading lines. tools/maths-type-test.cjs:497 test 20 with PAPER_DEBT.
body:
## Summary
The doc says maths-type-test "fails if it slips" under 28 px, but the gate read five script selectors; 23 rules under the floor were never checked.

## Description
docs/DESIGN-MATH-BUDDY.md:50 (law 8): nothing under 28 px except 20-22 px uppercase labels. tools/maths-type-test.cjs:300 (test 19) checks only the scripts and fraction parts - a hand-maintained list. A new 24 px sentence rule passed every gate. Built: test 20 reads every px font-size outside @media; under 28 it must be a 20-22 px label (uppercase on the rule or on the class the element carries). The paper screen's 7 under-floor reading lines are PAPER_DEBT, which may only shrink.

## Flow
- seed `.maths-tv .mb-seed { font-size: 24px }`
- HEAD suite: exit 0
- this suite: exit 1; bumping a PAPER_DEBT rule to 28 px: exit 1 until taken off the list

## Expected impact
A new under-floor line on a Math Buddy screen fails the desk gate. Could break: a deliberate 20-22 px label without uppercase must be uppercased or argued.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the ten-foot floor is gated for every rule
Before: seeded 24 px rule: HEAD maths-type-test exit 0; selectors the floor gate reads: 5
After: seeded rule exit 1; debt bump exit 1; selectors read: 96 (23 under the floor, 16 labels, 7 debt)
Method: gate - seeded controls, stylesheet restored byte for byte
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: MathsTV takes day from tv/day, not through the On Air screens module
evidence: desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx:33 (before) `import { day } from "@/tv/screens"`; desk/src/tv/screens.tsx:83 `export { day } from "@/tv/day"`. Probe (require MathsTV.tsx under tools/ts-load.cjs, 3 warm runs): 162 modules, qrcode loaded, 89-93 ms -> 86 modules, no qrcode, 61 ms. tools/maths-tv-test.cjs:1459 leaf.
body:
## Summary
One import of `day` through tv/screens pulled the whole On Air screens module (qrcode, recap, Linga and Essay pieces) into every load of Math Buddy's television.

## Description
desk/src/tv/screens.tsx:83 only re-exports day from tv/day.ts; desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx:33 imported it from screens. In the app page.tsx imports both anyway, so the bundle is unchanged; the cost is every suite and tool that loads MathsTV (server renders in maths-tv, maths-aim, paper-aim, tv-recap ...). Fixed: import from "@/tv/day"; a source guard pins it.

## Flow
- require MathsTV.tsx
- before: 162 modules incl. tv/screens and qrcode

## Expected impact
Faster maths suites, a narrower import graph. Could break nothing: the same function.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - fewer modules per MathsTV load
Before: 162 modules, 89-93 ms warm
After: 86 modules, 61 ms warm
Method: probe - require timing and require.cache count, three runs each side
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The paper screen's reading lines sit at 20-26 px, under Lamplight's 28 px floor
instrument: tools/maths-type-test.cjs test 20 PAPER_DEBT down to [] (the gate goes red per rule until listed rules reach 28 px), plus tools/maths-tv-test.cjs RP3 fit cases recomputed for OFF_NAME_PX 28 (desk/src/tv/paperRows.ts:207-209) and a Playwright capture of the paper screen (topics, off-desk, score card) on a second dev server
evidence: desk/src/design/maths-lamplight.css:698 .mb-prow .from 24px ("From 1, 3 · led by <statements>"); :705 .mb-poffrow .nm 26px; .mb-poffrow .lost 26px; .mb-poffrow .from 20px; :716 .mb-pscore .off 22px (offCountLine, leftOutLine sentences); .mb-poff .c 26px; :720 .mb-poff .m 22px (offSummary). desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx:741,757,772-779 put meaning in them.
body:
## Summary
Seven rules on the paper screen set meaning-carrying lines at 20-26 px, against docs/DESIGN-MATH-BUDDY.md law 8 (and On Air): only 20-22 px uppercase labels may sit under 28 px.

## Description
The From/led-by line (desk/src/design/maths-lamplight.css:698, 24 px), the off-desk statement name and lost marks (26 px), its From line (20 px), the score card's off and left-out sentences (:716, 22 px) and the Not on the desk lines (26 and 22 px, :720) are sentences, not labels (desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx:741,757,772-779). Raising them to 28 px changes the paper screen's fit: OFF_NAME_PX/OFF_NAME_ROOM (desk/src/tv/paperRows.ts:207-209) and the RP3 two-line guarantee move, and the score card may need a shorter column.

## Flow
- raise each PAPER_DEBT rule to 28 px
- recompute OFF_NAME_PX and the RP3 wrap cases; fix any overflow (fewer rows per window or a shorter line)
- take each rule off PAPER_DEBT as it reaches the floor
- capture the paper screen

## Expected impact
The learner on the sofa reads why the marks went at the size every other Math Buddy line reads. Could break: rows overflow their 104 px; the capture decides.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every paper-screen sentence at 28 px or more
Before: 7 meaning-carrying rules under 28 px (20, 22, 22, 24, 26, 26, 26)
After: predicted 0, PAPER_DEBT []; not built - a draw change with a fit to re-derive
Method: simulation - the RP3 fit arithmetic at 28 px: 732 px room / (0.55 x 28) = 47 characters a line vs 51 at 26, so some two-line statements become three; no dev server for a capture
Result: better
Gate: none

title: DESIGN-MATH-BUDDY sets the off-desk name at 26 px against its own 28 px law
evidence: docs/DESIGN-MATH-BUDDY.md:50 "nothing under 28 px except 20-22 px uppercase labels"; docs/DESIGN-MATH-BUDDY.md:491 "the name is 26 px in 732 px of room" (RP3, MB-B13); tools/maths-tv-test.cjs:1106 pins OFF_NAME_PX 26.
body:
## Summary
The design doc contradicts itself: law 8 floors text at 28 px, and the RP3 paragraph specifies the off-desk statement name at 26 px, which a test then pins.

## Description
docs/DESIGN-MATH-BUDDY.md:50 is the ten-foot law; docs/DESIGN-MATH-BUDDY.md:491 sets the off-desk name at 26 px so all 75 untouched statements wrap whole into two lines; tools/maths-tv-test.cjs:1106 pins 26. Either the law takes an exception for this row (and says so) or the row follows the law (the visual-craft card). Which one is the owner's design call, not a sweep's.

## Flow
- owner rules: exception or law
- exception: law 8 names the off-desk row; PAPER_DEBT keeps that one rule as allowed
- law: the visual-craft card is built

## Expected impact
A builder stops having to choose between two sentences of one doc. Could break nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one rule in the design doc
Before: 2 contradicting statements
After: 1, once the owner rules
Method: simulation - read both paragraphs and the pinning test; the decision has no figure
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: Removing a Paper row moves its picker's search and open areas onto the next row
instrument: a react-dom client test (act + a DOM shim, or Playwright on the phone page): type a search in row 1's picker, open an area, remove row 1, assert row 2's picker shows no search and is closed
evidence: desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx:86 `key={i}`; RowPicker keeps `query` in useState (desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx:47) and `<details>` holds its own open state; :93 Remove filters by index.
body:
## Summary
PaperPanel keys its rows by index, so removing a row hands its RowPicker state (search text, open areas) to the row that slides into its place.

## Description
Rows render with `key={i}` (desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx:86). The inputs are controlled, so values follow the data, but RowPicker's `query` state and the uncontrolled `<details>` open state stay with the index. Remove on row 1 (:93) leaves row 2 drawn with row 1's search and open areas. DraftRow has no id (rules/paperEntry, maths-school), so a stable key needs a panel-side id list kept in step with add, remove, restore and clear.

## Flow
- row 1: open the picker, type "fraction"
- remove row 1
- row 2 now shows "fraction" in its find box and row 1's open areas

## Expected impact
The picker shows the row's own state after a removal. Could break: restore or clear from the page must reset the id list.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - picker state belongs to its row
Before: walked: remove row 1 of 2 - row 2 inherits 2 pieces of state (query, open details)
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - React reconciliation by key walked on three cases (remove first, remove middle, remove last: the last case is unaffected); no DOM harness in the rules suites
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Every paper move and ruler move runs its whole fit twice
instrument: a counter on lay()/fit() per dependency change (a fake document.fonts with status "loaded" and a resolved ready), then the stick: tools/stick-perf window.mjs longest frame gap on Walk Left/Right and Topics Left/Right, before and after
evidence: desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx:197-199 usePaper: lay(); then document.fonts?.ready.then(lay); :379-381 useNameFit: fit(); then ready.then(fit). Deps change on every focus move (:934 Sheet `${ix}|...`, :976 Walk `${s.walkIx}|...`, :320 Ruler `${path}|${focus}`).
body:
## Summary
usePaper and useNameFit lay out, then lay out again on document.fonts.ready, which is an already-resolved promise once the faces are in: two full fits per D-pad move.

## Description
desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx:197-199 and :379-381 run the fit, then schedule it again on `document.fonts.ready`. After the first load the promise is resolved, so the second pass runs as a microtask in the same frame: every row is reset and re-measured (fitRows forces a reflow per scrollWidth read, :228). The dependencies change on every move on the Sheet, the Walk, Units and the Topics ruler. A guard - re-run only when `document.fonts.status !== "loaded"` after the first pass - halves the work, but a face that starts loading during the first pass must still trigger the second, which only the stick can confirm.

## Flow
- build the counter instrument; show 2 passes per move
- guard the second pass on fonts.status
- take the stick figure on Walk and Topics moves; keep only if the frame gap does not grow and the fit matches

## Expected impact
Less main-thread layout per move on the stick. Could break: a line fitted with fallback metrics if a face loads late and status misreports.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - one fit pass per move
Before: 2 passes per move (code read: lay() then ready.then(lay))
After: predicted 1 pass; stick frame gap unmeasured
Method: simulation - three moves walked (Sheet Right, Walk Right, Topics Right): each re-runs fitRows or fitName twice; no stick in this run
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Eleven aria-labels on generic spans and divs that a screen reader may drop
instrument: axe-core aria-prohibited-attr count on a server-rendered Sheet, Walk and Tonight (jsdom or Playwright), then a VoiceView pass on the stick reading the tally and a pen mark
evidence: desk/src/maths/MathText.tsx:52,54,62,65,136,146,149,155 aria-label on <b>/<span> with no role; desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx:338 .mb-slips div, :535 hero .tally span, :852 .mb-tally div; compare desk/src/maths/MathsCollection.tsx:30 and desk/src/maths/Plot.tsx:13, which add role="img".
body:
## Summary
Math Buddy names its pen marks, the tallies and the slip scratches with aria-label on elements with no role, which ARIA 1.2 prohibits and screen readers may ignore.

## Description
Eleven sites put aria-label on a generic span/div/b (desk/src/maths/MathText.tsx:52-155, eight; desk/src/maths/MathsTV.tsx:338, :535, :852). Two sibling sites do it right with role="img" (desk/src/maths/MathsCollection.tsx:30, desk/src/maths/Plot.tsx:13). The pen marks are the picture of the verdict on the TV; if VoiceView drops the names, a learner using it hears the maths without the desk's mark. Fix: role="img" on the eleven (the inner glyphs are already aria-hidden or text).

## Flow
- run axe on the rendered Sheet: count aria-prohibited-attr
- add role="img" at the eleven sites
- axe again; VoiceView on the stick reads "the wrong sign"

## Expected impact
A VoiceView user hears where the desk's pen is. Could break: role="img" hides the inner text of a mark from AT, so the label must carry it (it does at each site).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every named mark is exposed to assistive tech
Before: 11 prohibited aria-label sites, 2 correct siblings
After: predicted 0; VoiceView effect unmeasured
Method: simulation - the ARIA rule checked against code; no axe or VoiceView in the rules suites
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: Remove this question is a ~20 px tap target that deletes a row with no undo
instrument: a Playwright phone-viewport capture of the Paper panel measuring the button box (getBoundingClientRect height) before and after; an undo or confirm decided with the owner
evidence: desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx:93 `<button className="plink" ...>Remove this question</button>` directly under the RowPicker; desk/src/app/globals.css:60 `.plink { padding: 0; font: inherit; ... }`; the panel's inputs are 44 px (desk/src/app/globals.css:56).
body:
## Summary
The Paper panel's destructive Remove link has no padding (text height only) and sits right under the statement picker, so a slipped tap deletes a typed question with nothing to bring it back.

## Description
`.plink` (desk/src/app/globals.css:60, phone-surface's stylesheet) has padding 0, so the target is the text line, about 20 px, under the 44 px the panel's own inputs use (:56). In PaperPanel (desk/src/app/phone/PaperPanel.tsx:93) it follows the picker's checkbox list, where the thumb works. A removed row is gone: no undo. Fix: a 44 px target in the panel (its own class) and either an undo line or a confirm.

## Flow
- type a question with three statements picked
- scroll the picker; the thumb lands on Remove
- the row is gone

## Expected impact
Fewer lost rows while typing a paper on a phone. Could break nothing; the undo shape is a product choice.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the destructive control meets the panel's 44 px target
Before: target height ~20 px (padding 0, inherited font)
After: predicted 44 px; not measured (no browser here)
Method: simulation - computed from the stylesheet; globals.css is phone-surface's
Result: better
Gate: none
